facts.text: QuadrupedEnv is constructed from a robot name and defaults to the flat scene, the default observation names, sim_dt 0.002 s, the forward velocity command of 0.5 m/s and 0.0 rad/s, ground friction 1.0 and the leg order FL, FR, RL, RR
The default observations are qpos, qvel, tau_ctrl_setpoint, feet_pos:base and feet_vel:base
The observation space is a gymnasium Dict of Box bounds built from the model's joint ranges and actuator control ranges
The action space is a gymnasium Box of shape (mjModel.nu,): one torque per actuator, with low and high taken from actuator_forcerange
The scene model is loaded from robot_model/scene_<scene>.xml and its terrain is generated for the robot's hip height
The go2 robot configuration uses robot_model/go2/go2.xml and a hip height of 0.28 m
The simulation timestep is the sim_dt constructor argument and is assigned to mjModel.opt.timestep
A step writes the action to mjData.ctrl, advances MuJoCo with one mj_step and then steps every configured sensor
A step returns the observation, reward, terminated, truncated and info; info carries time, step_num and invalid_contacts
An episode terminates on an invalid contact or on leaving the terrain bounds; step never truncates
A random reset adds white noise of +-20 degrees to joint positions and +-0.5 to joint velocities around the model keyframe, with an options angle_sweep override for the position amplitude
reset(seed) seeds numpy's global random generator
reset returns the observation dictionary from _get_obs()
A reset randomizes the ground tangential friction coefficient from the configured ground_friction_coeff range
close() closes the viewer if one was opened and clears it

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds numpy's global generator at quadruped_env.py:348-349, so one MuJoCo build repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the package's fake draws the initial perturbation with Python's random.Random, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: rigid-body MuJoCo dynamics with contacts and a terrain generated from the scene, but no actuator, sensor or noise model beyond a direct torque command: F2 is not claimed
the fake backend is a pure Python stand-in: it has no contacts, friction, actuator model, sensors or terrain, and its one scalar integration step does not reproduce MuJoCo's equations of motion
the fake never terminates or truncates: the upstream invalid-contact and out-of-terrain checks are not modelled
the fake's initial state is perturbed with Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's global generator, so the same seed does not replay the same trajectory on both
no physical quadruped is modelled and the environment was never validated against one: F3 is not claimed

the upstream environment was not imported where the gate ran (mujoco, numpy, scipy and gymnasium are not installed for the gate), so the fake was not compared with the upstream simulator and the sim backend was not run

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state stays readable
